headline: Quiet day, just one small signal
summary: No new models or big tools dropped. Only news: Replit's desktop app landed Christie's thanks to its security setup

items.title: Replit desktop app is all about security, and Christie's is already using it
items.what: Replit is a platform where AI helps you write code and build apps, and now it has a desktop version. Reportedly, on Windows it runs each AI-generated app in its own "sandbox" (a locked-off safe little room), so it can't mess with other files on your computer. Replit CEO Amjad Masad says the security model was built together with the Windows team, and that Christie's (the old-school art auction house) picked it for "secure agent work".
items.meaning: This is mostly Replit marketing and doesn't affect you much right now. But "AI desktop apps need locked-down permissions" is going to be a bigger and bigger trend.
actions: If you want to try the Windows version, check replit.com/desktop to see if it's open yet (reportedly it's a waitlist preview for now)
deep_dive: Compared to Claude Code and codex that you use: those run right on your computer, and you're the one watching permissions. Replit's approach locks each build in a sandbox.
Known gaps so far: Replit hasn't shared the default sandbox rules, the official launch date, hardware requirements, or pricing.
The details of Christie's usage (what for, how deeply) come from just one tweet by Masad, with no third-party confirmation.
items.signals: Amjad Masad tweet 201 likes · Customer case: Christie's · No third-party testing
